    Cameras shift color with their own white balance and exposure. For a truer reading, put the crosshair on a Neutral 5 card in the same light and tap Calibrate on N 5.

    Cross planes · value 9 to 1Tap a plane to see it alone on the tree.
    Pigment Current mix Mixing path Ground

    Each square is a pixel sampled from the painting, placed by its Munsell hue, value and chroma, so the cloud shows the painting's color harmony: which hues it uses, how far its chroma reaches, and where its values cluster. Zoom in for a finer sample, and tap any square to see that color and where it appears in the painting. Photos shift color with light and camera, so read the shape of the harmony rather than exact notations.

    The trunk is the neutral value scale, black at the base to white at the top. Mixing paths curve through the tree and bend toward the trunk: two pigments rarely mix along a straight line, and complements cancel to neutral. Switch the cloud to the mix's pigments to see how each pigment you add pushes the reachable area outward.

    Map the mixes

    Tap the picture to add a location of your own, such as a cheek, a knuckle or the shadow side of a collar.

    With a free account, hovering a location also lights its spot on the Munsell tree, and you can print the key as a handout.

      Munsell Book

      40 hue pages · value up · chroma out
      Tap a chip to see its notation and the closest mix from your palette.

      Each page holds one hue, with value rising from 1 to 9 and chroma stepping out by 2 from the neutral. The chips are converted from the Munsell renotation data (the 1943 measurements behind modern Munsell books), and a page shows only what a screen can display; the colors are a guide, not a substitute for a physical Munsell book.

      Wavelength

      The visible spectrum · what the mix reflects

      Wavelength (nanometers) · bright = light the mix reflects, dark = light it absorbs
      Registers as
      —
      Purity
      —
      Reflects most
      —
      Absorbs most
      —

      Paint mixes by subtraction. Each pigment absorbs part of the spectrum, and the mix keeps only the light that all of its pigments reflect. The wavelength it registers as is the single spectral color the eye matches its hue to. Purples have no single wavelength, so they are named by their complement, marked with a c.

      Light, paint, eye

      The lamp sends every color of its light out in every direction. Light that misses the sphere flies past or lands on the floor; where the sphere blocks it, the floor is left in shadow. Of the light that reaches the sphere, a little of all of it bounces straight off the glossy surface, which is why the highlight takes the color of the lamp. The rest enters the paint, where the pigments absorb some wavelengths and send others back out. Those are the colors you see. Slide to follow the light from the lamp to your eye, and warm the lamp to watch the same paint change color.

      Colors come from a spectral pigment model (Kubelka–Munk mixing over 31 wavelength bands), so mixtures darken and dull the way paint does rather than averaging like light. Oleogel is modeled as a perfectly clear medium: it adds no color, it only spreads the pigment thinner in a film of fixed thickness, so the ground shows through. Hiding is measured the way a drawdown card does it, by comparing the film over black with the film over white. The reachable-colors cloud samples every pair of pigments at many ratios, every set of three (when the set is small enough to compute quickly) and several amounts of white, all at full strength. Munsell notation is estimated from CIELAB and rounded to 2.5 hue steps; real tubes vary by brand, oil and load, so treat the numbers as a guide and check against a physical Munsell chart.

      Community Guidelines

      A few simple promises that keep this a good place to learn, for everyone.

      1. Be kind. Critique the painting, never the person.
      2. Share your own work. Upload only images you made or have permission to use. You keep all rights to your work.
      3. Keep it safe. No harassment, hate or explicit content, and no one else’s personal details.
      4. Respect the teaching. Studio videos and lessons are for your own learning. Please don’t copy, record, share or resell them.
      5. Color is a guide. Readings depend on screens, cameras and light. Use them alongside your own eye.
      6. Your privacy. Your account keeps only your email, to sign you in. It is never sold or shared. Paintings you upload stay on your own device.
      7. 13 or older. You must be at least 13 to create an account.
      8. A growing community. Features and membership may change as the platform grows. Members will be told before any paid plan begins.
      9. Fair play. Content or accounts that break these guidelines may be removed.
